title: The mirror up to nature. (He laughs.) Hu hu hu hu hu hu.
html_source: Hamlet again. This time it’s from the mini-play The Mousetrap. What we’ve just seen is intentionally over-the-top vulgar and cruel. Hamlet advises the cast caution against overacting. “For anything so overdone is from [contrary to] the purpose of playing, whose end, both at the first and now, was and is, to hold, as ’t were, a mirror up to nature; to show virtue her own feature, scorn her own [nature’s] image and the very age and body of the time his form and pressure.” The scene just endured here in Circe is seemingly overwrought, and laden with inflated distaste so as to hold up a mirror to, and scorn, unconstrained nature, the image of that age in Ireland, the form of the times. We can conclude, then, that if what has been displayed in the scene is not exaggerated, but is intended as an accurate portrayal of contemporary Irish culture, then it is not, in fact, overacting.
